previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of bioprosthetic aortic valve, pacemaker, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, chronic diastolic heart failure, and recurrent cellulitis was admitted for rapidly progressive right leg erythema and pain, consistent with cellulitis, despite being on suppressive cephalexin. She presented with fever and developed septic shock requiring vasopressors and ICU care. Blood cultures grew Morganella, and imaging ruled out necrotizing infection and DVT. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, transitioned to vancomycin and meropenem, and discharged on a two-week course of IV ertapenem via PICC line. Due to a subtherapeutic INR of 1.8 and recent TIA history, she was bridged with Lovenox. Her renal dysfunction resolved, and she improved clinically, returning to baseline home medications. She was discharged home with home health support for IV antibiotics and follow-up arranged.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  DX BILATERAL ANKLES

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with recurrent cellulitis who p/w worsening
erythema and pain and is now on abx. please eval for osteomyelitis on right
ankle and left ankle/lower leg where wounds are located.  // Please evaluate
for right and left ankle and left shin for signs of osteomyelitis (where her
wounds are located)     Please evaluate for right and left ankle and left shin
for signs of osteomyelitis (where her wounds are located)

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal, oblique, and lateral view radiographs of both ankles

COMPARISON:  None available.

FINDINGS: 

Soft tissue swelling is present in the left lower extremity extending to the
level of the ankle.  There is no evidence of acute fracture or dislocation at
either ankle, and there are no radiographic findings to suggest osteomyelitis
at these sites.  Marked degenerative changes are present in the midfoot region
bilaterally and at the talonavicular joint on the right as well as findings
consistent with previous talonavicular arthrodesis.  Bones are diffusely
demineralized.

IMPRESSION: 

No conventional radiographic findings of osteomyelitis.  MRI would be more
sensitive and may be considered for further evaluation if warranted
clinically.
